providers.title: Markov type bounds sums of odd edge labels
providers.scope: Let V have Markov type p with constant K. For a finite stationary reversible marked chain with edges E_1, E_2, ... and a labeling g of the edges with g(e*) = -g(e): E |g(E_1) + ... + g(E_n)|^p <= K^p n E |g(E_1)|^p. The labels need not be differences of a function of the states.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A finite form of Goldstine's theorem
providers.scope: For w in the bidual of Y with norm at most 1, functionals f_1, ..., f_i and eps > 0 there is y in Y with norm at most 1 and |f_h(y) - w(f_h)| <= eps for all h.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sequences that control partial sums in a nonreflexive space
providers.scope: Let Y be a nonreflexive real Banach space and 0 < d < 1. For every M there are z_1, ..., z_M of norm at most 1 with d max_j |a_1 + ... + a_j| - (1/M) sum |a_h| <= |sum a_h z_(i_h)| <= sum |a_h| for all i_1 < ... < i_m and all real a_h.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The ordered norm
providers.scope: Assume (JE) (James and Enflo; not proved in the programme). If a real Banach space X is not superreflexive, there is a norm N on finitely supported sequences that is spreading invariant, for which merging two adjacent entries does not increase the norm, and such that every (R^m, N) embeds linearly into X with distortion arbitrarily close to 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A law on charts that treats all tuples alike
providers.scope: For a finite ordered set and eps > 0 there are B and a distribution on the strictly increasing maps C into {1..B} such that the laws of C(A) and C(A') are within eps in total variation for any two increasing tuples A, A' of the same length.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Maximal coupling
providers.scope: Two distributions on a finite set have a coupling whose diagonal has mass 1 - TV.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reversible transport of charts
providers.scope: For partial order isomorphisms T_s of a finite ordered set, indexed by a set with a fixed-point-free involution and T_(s^-1) = T_s^-1, and eps > 0: there is a finite stationary reversible marked chain on charts whose letters are independent and uniform and whose every step (C, s, C') satisfies C'(a) = C(T_s(a)) on the domain of T_s with probability at least 1 - eps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The reduced length of a random word
providers.scope: For n independent uniform letters from {u, v, u^-1, v^-1} the reduced length l satisfies E l >= n/2 and P(l >= n/4) >= 1/4.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Four homeomorphisms of the line that play ping-pong
providers.scope: For four disjoint closed intervals in (0,1), indexed by u, v, u^-1, v^-1, with periodic arcs A_s: there are increasing homeomorphisms h_s of the line with h_s(y+1) = h_s(y)+1, h_(s^-1) = h_s^-1, h_s(R minus A_(s^-1)) = A_s and |h_s(y) - y| < 2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two levels
providers.scope: For a word w with reduced form of length l > 0 with n_+ positive and n_- negative letters, the sum c_w of the functions chi_s along the backward orbit satisfies c_w(j) = -n_- and c_w(h_w(0) + j) = n_+ for all integers j.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A reversible walk with linear displacement
providers.scope: Let N be a spreading invariant norm on finitely supported sequences with contractive merging. For every n there are a finite stationary reversible marked chain and an odd labeling g with N(g(e)) = 1 for all edges such that N(g(E_1) + ... + g(E_n)) >= n/24 with probability at least 3/20. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nontrivial Markov type forces superreflexivity
providers.scope: Assume (JE). Every real Banach space with Markov type p for some p > 1 has an equivalent uniformly convex norm.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
